requirements.text: The cap of the LED light source shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
The cap of the LED light source shall bear the rated voltage.
The cap of the LED light source shall bear the designation of the relevant category.
The cap of the LED light source shall bear a space of sufficient size to accommodate the approval mark.
The LED light source shall be so designed as to be and to remain in good working order when in normal use.
The LED light source shall exhibit no fault in design or manufacture.
The LED light source shall exhibit no scores or spots on its optical surfaces which might impair its efficiency and its optical performance.
The LED light source shall be equipped with a standard cap complying with the cap data sheet of IEC Publication 60061 as specified on its data sheet of Annex 1.
The cap shall be strong and firmly secured to the rest of the LED light source.
The solid state junction(s) and possibly one or more elements for fluorescence-based conversion shall be the only elements of the LED light source that generate and emit light when energized.
The LED light source shall first be aged at its test voltage for at least forty-eight hours.
Unless otherwise specified, electrical and photometric measurements of the LED light source shall be carried out at the relevant test voltage(s).
Electrical measurements as specified in Annex 4 shall be carried out with instruments of at least class 0.2 (0.2 per cent full scale accuracy).
The position and dimensions of the light emitting area shall conform to the requirements given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.
When measured according to the conditions specified in Annex 4, the luminous flux shall be within the limits given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.

When measured according to the test conditions specified in Annex 4, the normalized luminous intensity distribution and/or cumulative luminous flux distribution shall be within the limits given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.
The colour of the light emitted by the LED light source shall be as specified on the relevant data sheet, applying the colour definitions of UN Regulation No. 48.
The colour of the light emitted shall be measured by the method specified in Annex 4.
The measured integral value of the chromaticity coordinates of the emitted light shall lie within the required chromaticity area.
The UV-radiation of the LED light source shall be such that the LED light source is of the low UV type.
At the maximum test temperature specified on the data sheet, the luminous flux values at elevated temperatures shall be within the limits given in the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.
At the maximum test temperature specified on the data sheet, the colour variation shall not exceed 0.010.

After the measurement at the maximum test temperature, the LED light source shall be continuously operated during 1000 h at the relevant test voltage(s), with an integrated heat sink at an ambient temperature corresponding to the maximum test temperature of the data sheet.
After the 1000 h operation the luminous flux values at elevated temperatures shall not deviate by more than ± 10 per cent from the values of the same sample measured before the operation.
After the 1000 h operation the colour variation shall not deviate from the values of the same sample measured before the operation by more than ± 0.010.
After the measurements following the 1000 h operation, the LED light source shall again exhibit no scores or spots on its optical surfaces as required in paragraph 3.2.3.
